persona: Same field biologist, running monthly stream water-quality and macroinvertebrate monitoring at 3 stations across a field season, kept as a running workbook with one tab added per month
source_style: hand-entered into Excel from a paper field notebook after each monthly sampling trip, workbook grown incrementally month to month without going back to standardize earlier tabs

intended_analysis: Do stream temperature, pH, and dissolved oxygen differ among the 3 stations and change across the May-July sampling season, and how does macroinvertebrate taxa richness relate to those water-quality variables?
mess_applied: two-row merged header on the May sheet ('Water Quality Parameters' spans D1:F1 over Water Temp C/pH/DO mg/L) -- the real header is row 2
the same temperature variable is spelled 3 different ways across the workbook's 3 monthly sheets: 'Water Temp C' (May), 'Temp C' (June), 'Temp (C)' (July)
one date on the May sheet is stored as the ambiguous text '5/3' (no year) while the other rows for the identical calendar day are real Excel date values
station names are inconsistently capitalized/spaced within the June sheet: 'Site 1', 'SITE 2', 'Site 3', 'site 1', 'Site 2 ' (trailing space) all denote the same handful of stations

missing values are coded 4 different ways across the workbook: blank/true-empty (July DO), 'n/a' text (May DO), '-' text (July pH), and simply omitting the row entirely (June has no Site 3 row on 6/17 at all)
a non-sample 'AVG' summary row is appended directly below the real data on the May sheet, inside the same contiguous data block
blank separator rows appear inside the data block on the May and June sheets
a full-width merged note row ('Site 3 flooded after storm - no sample collected 6/17') sits inside the June data block explaining a missing observation; it is not itself a data record
the June sheet has a stray column (F) with no header and no values at all, wedged between pH and DO mg/L
half of July's temperature values (the 7/22 batch) are stored as text with a trailing unit, e.g. '20.1 C', while the 7/8 batch is plain numeric in the same column
an accidental duplicate data entry on the July sheet: the Site 1, 7/8 row appears twice with identical values
a separate 'Site Key' reference sheet (station descriptions and coordinates) sits in the same workbook as the 3 monthly data sheets and is not itself data
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A naive reader would likely ingest the May AVG row and June's merged flood-note row as real observations, misread June's blank column F as a genuine (empty) variable, silently drop or mis-parse the text date '5/3' and the unit-suffixed July temperatures ('20.1 C') as non-numeric/NaN, fail to recognize 'Site 1'/'site 1'/'SITE 2'/'Site 2 ' as the same 2-3 stations (inflating the apparent number of groups), and double-count the duplicated July Site 1 (7/8) row when computing station means or sample sizes.
